paper_title: Ultralight Dark Matter Search with Space-Time Separated Atomic Clocks and Cavities
notes: Paper presents NEW measured exclusion limits on scalar dark matter coupling to electron mass (d_me) using space-time separated atomic clocks and optical cavities. Two independent analyses: (1) NPL/PTB cavity comparison over 2220 km fiber link probing spatial fluctuations; (2) GPS satellite microwave clocks probing temporal fluctuations. Mass range: 10^-19 to 2×10^-15 eV. These are stated as 'the first constraints on d_me alone in this mass range.' The coupling values are extracted from Fig. 2 (right panel) which shows the exclusion limits as a roughly horizontal band at log10|d_me| ≈ -4.8 to -5.0 across the mass range. Converted to linear scale: ~1.3-1.6 × 10^-5. Used 1.5e-5 as representative value. The paper uses κ = √(4π)/M_Pl normalization for d_me (dimensionless). DM density of 0.4 GeV/cm³ is standard assumption stated in text for field amplitude calculation. Confidence level is 95% as stated throughout.
